## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

All comparison arms below used candidate `108b7f3cde06b8c80594ee2ea54df0b51122fabf` / tree `c4183673738e11f68d99c8d914d6badca458d37c`, except the explicitly identified BASE reproduction. These arms used the same AlmaLinux 9 FreeIPA / Ubuntu 24.04 native services as the fresh chain, with real Wazuh containers. Before the BASE/candidate comparison the two owned VMs were restored to the same healthy enrolled-client + Wazuh snapshot.

| Arm | Observed result |
|---|---|
| BASE `07f55a6e11cb39be0988e3b032bfa144ed5ec387`, Wazuh first, default 8443 | apply ok=51 changed=16 failed=1; curl rc=60 after five attempts; journal reports `address already in use`; Wazuh docker-proxy owns 8443; IPA cert is MONITORING |
| Candidate, Wazuh first, default 18443 | syntax/check/apply/verify/idempotency pass; L3 ok=45 changed=12, L4 ok=57 changed=16; 27/27 verify, zero skips; L6 ok=54 changed=0 |
| Candidate, explicit port 28443 | syntax/check/apply/verify/idempotency pass; L3 ok=46 changed=1, L4 ok=56 changed=2; 27/27 verify, zero skips; L6 ok=54 changed=0 |
| Request occupied 8443 with `SS_service` selected | early preflight exits 2, changed=0 failed=1; config/binary/helper/FQDN hashes, store MainPID/InvocationID and Wazuh container identity unchanged |
| Expected FQDN changed while trusted cert and real store stay healthy | exact SS02 command exits 1 with curl rc=60 hostname mismatch; restoring FQDN makes it pass |
| Different PID presents the real IPA-trusted cert on a separate listener | direct TLS control returns HTTP 401; SS02 helper rejects ownership while the real store remains active; config restored and helper passes |
| Wazuh functionality with both listeners present | native indexer HTTP 401 and `wazuh-logtest` known-alert checks pass, both before fresh teardown and in the Wazuh-first/custom-port environment |

The different-PID HTTPS server is an explicit negative fixture, not another real session store. Its temporary config changes and unit were removed/restored before the next chain. The final fresh chain above is the opposite installation order: session-store before Wazuh. Both owned VMs were automatically torn down successfully.

An earlier run of this same candidate failed closed with `certificate is not yet valid` after snapshot-related guest clock skew; single-VM automatic rollback completed. The first publication attempt also refused an unmanaged initial LATEST placeholder. Only mutable evidence output was cleared in the archive; execution files were unchanged. The complete chain was rerun successfully after synchronizing both owned guests to controller UTC following the snapshot. This time synchronization was an external fixture, not a TLS exception. The fresh chain also records verified UTC synchronization. A preliminary single-host enrollment attempt was rejected because its inventory lacked the required FreeIPA-server group; the supported grouped inventory corrected that setup failure before comparison runs.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

- This is a focused site-order wrapper containing FreeIPA server, canonical client fixtures, client enrollment, Docker, session-store and Wazuh; it is not a full `site.yml` deployment of unrelated roles.
- Only the committed session-store spec was verified as a whole (27/27). Many existing rows are `true` placeholders for delegated unit/structural properties. The new native proof is listener ownership, configured-hostname/CA TLS, coexistence and idempotency; it does not newly prove every property named by those placeholder rows.
- Wazuh SIEM forwarding was not configured, so C10/C11 and full Wazuh 11-row verification are not claimed. The native indexer, rule engine, containers and listener coexistence were checked.
- Gateway-to-store recording/replay, HA/replicas, production capacity, other client OS versions and real-host deployment were not rerun. The test host had 6 GiB RAM/4 vCPU/40 GiB disk; this is not a Wazuh production-sizing claim.
- Preflight observes but does not reserve a socket. The native wrong-owner arm and real-socket harness exercise rejection; no natural bind race is claimed. The standalone playbook still has no general mutation rollback. The observed rollback was the single-VM test harness after the clock/TLS failure, not a newly implemented playbook rescue or a multi-node recovery proof.
- SS02 proves the local listener and TLS identity using `--resolve`; it does not prove external DNS/routing or authenticated PIT1 ingest. Existing gateway URLs require coordinated migration to 18443, or an explicit legacy port on a host where it is free.
- Dynamic Ansible dependencies listed above remain unresolved for automatic evidence reuse. These are exact-candidate runs; no advanced-base or cross-candidate reuse is claimed.
